summary: The root كُلْأَةٌ (kulʾah) refers to pasturage or herbage, something that is guarded or preserved. It is related to the idea of protection and sustenance for livestock.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: (S, K,) aor. كَلَاَ, inf. n. كَلْءٌ (K) and كِلَآءَةٌ (S, K) and كِلَآءٌ (K) [but respecting this last see a verse of Jemeel cited below], He (i. e. God, S) guarded him, or kept him, or kept him safely. (S, K.) إِ ْهَبُوا فِى كِلَآءَةِ اللّٰهِ Go ye in the safe keeping of God.

inf. n. تَكْلِىْءٌ and تَكْلِئَةٌ, He brought a ship near to the bank of the river, (K,) and moored it. (TA.) كلّأ (assumed tropical:) He retained, detained, or confined, a person: (K:) app. from the verb as used with reference to a ship; and therefore tropical. (TA.) كلّأ, (K,) inf. n. تَكْلِىْءٌ, (TA,) He came to a place, and stopped there. (TA.) كلّأ, inf. n. تَكْلِئَةٌ, He came to a place sheltered from the wind. (S) كلّأ He came to a person (K) on an affair.
inf. n. مُكَالَأَةٌ, and كِلَأءٌ, He watched, or observed. (TA.)

أَكْلَاَ See 1 in three places. اكلأت عَيْنُهُ (tropical:) His eye was sleepless, or wakeful. (A.) اكلأ عَيْنَهُ, and, (tropical:) He made his eye sleepless, or wakeful. (A.) اكلأ عُمُرَهُ (tropical:) He brought his life to its close. (K.) See 1.

; and, inf. n. تَكْلِىْءٌ; He bought on credit. [This is the explanation given in the TK, and it appears to be correct. It is also there said, that تَكَلَّأْتُهُ signifies أَخَ ْتُهُ نَسْيْئَةً, I took it, or bought it, on credit: and كَلَّأْتُ فِى الطَّعَامِ, اخ ته بالنّسيئةِ, I took, or bought, the food on credit, but the latter I render differently.

اكتلأ مِنْهُ (assumed tropical:) He preserved, or guarded, himself from him or it; had a care of, or was cautious of, him or it. (S, K. *) اكتلأت عَيْنى (assumed tropical:) My eye was wakeful, vigilant, or cautious. (S.) اكتلأ كُلْأَةً, and, He received a كُلْأَة [i. e., an earnest, or money paid in advance ]. (K.)

Fresh herbage; syn. عُشْبٌ: (S, K:) applied to the عُرْوَة, نصِىّ, and صِلِّيَان: (Az:) or pasture, or what cattle &c. feed upon: (TA:) or herbage. whether fresh or dry either fresh pasture or fodder: (S, K:) or it comprises the صِلَّيَان نَصِىّ, حَلَمَة, شِيح, عَرْفَج, the various kinds of عُرْوَة, and what are termed عُشْب, بَقْل, and the like: or it is applied to the herbs called بقل, and to trees: a gen. n., having no sing.; or its sing. is كَلَآءٌ. (TA.)

أَرْضٌ كَلِئَةٌ , (S, K,) and, (K,) and, (S,) A land containing, (S,) or abounding with, (K,) كَلَأ, or herbage. (S, K.) The ↓ last is also said to signify A land with the pasture of which its camels have been satiated. (TA.) See a trad. quoted in art. فَضْلٌ.

عَيْنٌ كَلُوْءٌ (tropical:) A strong eye, which sleep does not overcome. (TA.) كَلُوْءٌ العَيْنِ (tropical:) A man, or a camel, (male or female,) having a strong eye, which sleep does not overcome: (K:) or, a sleepless, or wakeful, eye. (A.) مَرْأَةٌ كَلُوْءُ اللَّيْلِ (tropical:) [ A woman who is sleepless at night ]. (TA.) See 4.

and A station of ships, (S, K,) near the bank of a river, or near what is called the جُدّ: (TA:) the former is masc. and fem.; or, accord. to Sb, it is of the measure فَعَّالٌ; and therefore masc., and perfectly declinable: (S:) so called because it keeps the vessels safe ( يَكْلَؤُهَا ) from the wind: but accord.

(S, K) and (K) i. q. نَسِيْئَةٌ, [app. bearing both of the two significations immediately following, and clearly shown in the S &c. to bear the latter of them: A postponement, or delay, in the time of the payment of a debt, &c. See also نُسْأَةٌ, and كَلَأَ. Also, both words, like نَسِيْئَةٌ, A debt of which the payment is deferred by a creditor to a future period. ] (S, K.) Ex., نَهَى عَنِ الكَالِئِ بِالكَالِئ, i.

(tropical:) Longer, or longest; more, or most, protracted. (TA.) بَلَغَ اللّٰهُ بِكَ أَكْلَأَ العُمُرِ (S, A) i. e. (tropical:) [ May God cause thee to reach, or attain, ] the extreme, or most distant, period of life! (S, TA.)
للْعَيْنِ فِيهَا مَكْلُوْءٌ (tropical:) The eye is constantly fixed upon her: [or has in her an object that is watched ( by it ):] as though watching her because pleased with her. (A.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
